headline: CogGym reports a large matched human–model evaluation suite with persistent behavioral gaps
summary: A September 18 preprint introduces CogGym, a human-in-the-loop pipeline that standardizes cognitive-science experiments into a common format for matched human and language-model evaluation. The initial release reports 258 experiments from 100 papers across text, image and video, with 50 language models evaluated. On the paper’s reported human–model fit measure, the best models reach R² of 0.59 for text, 0.58 for image and 0.43 for video, below estimated human split-half references of 0.93, 0.95 and 0.92. A 15-experiment replication with 521 participants reports closer agreement between new and original human responses than between Gemini 3.1 Pro and the original responses. These are author-reported results; the 15-study check is a subset, not an independent reproduction of the full suite.
